context: A bandit (Warryn) has come upon the body of a companion who was crushed by a falling boulder; the death reads as an accident rather than a fight. Warryn's response is more grumbling and complaint than deep grief, reacting to the practical horror of the situation. Nothing in the scene implies recent combat—this is an environmental hazard—and the tone is pragmatic, matching other short, blunt reactions characters have when they find corpses. While characters in similar scenes might loot or brood, this particular exchange focuses on Warryn's exasperated, resigned response to the accident.
